# Dark-Model Fidelity Triage

> Historical note (2026-06-10): references to `frontier-state.yaml` below
> predate the autonomy demolition. That ledger is retired. Its issue-tagged
> evidence moved to `backlog-archive.md` (grep `#NNN`), the rest to
> `tas-era-ledger.md`. Read "frontier-state.yaml audience" as "the backlog".

The [dead-helper census](dead-helper-census.md) mapped ~2540 ASM-faithful, unit-tested helpers carrying `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` that are never wired into the live runtime. The census answered what is dark. This triage answers the question it did not: which dark subsystems close a real oracle divergence (worth wiring) versus which have a live fallback that is already oracle-clean (redundant, leave dark).

Method: one read-only investigator per subsystem (confirm still-dark, find live fallback, read cited ASM, judge oracle divergence, sketch minimal wiring), then an adversarial refuter tries to refute every divergence claim. The refuter is the guard against mistaking "model is dark" for "fallback is wrong". Ranked by fidelity leverage (confirmed > suspected > unknown > clean), lowest effort first.

Bottom line: 3 of 13 dark subsystems survive scrutiny as worth-wiring. The refuter demoted 6 to redundant (fallback already oracle-clean); wiring those would be wasted effort.

### 1. blocks (metal-block push / lift-block bob / ice-block bullets)  `[SUSPECTED diverges]`

- **id**: `blocks-metal-lift-ice` · **status**: partially_wired · **risk**: medium · **effort**: medium · **refuter verdict**: True (medium)
- **backlog**: #128, #067, #232, #149, #242, #213, #218
- **ASM**: loc_111F4, loc_11208, loc_11230, loc_1125C, sub_1129C, loc_112E2, loc_112FE, loc_11328, loc_11358, sub_FB3E, loc_FB94, loc_FBA2, loc_FBB0, loc_FBBE
- **dead entrypoint**: Metal push: NativeRuntime::metal_block_push_entry_loc_111F4 / metal_block_push_step_right_loc_112E2 / metal_block_push_step_left_loc_112FE + struct MetalBlockPushWakeStep, crates/wildside-core/src/blocks.rs:363,3762,3845,3862 (all #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))], only referenced from tests/runtime_tests.rs:7206-7516). Lift bob: NativeRuntime::lift_block_bob_deltas_sub_FB3E + lift_block_bob_up/down_pass_loc_FB94..FBDA, blocks.rs:3411-3473 (only tests/runtime_tests.rs:10389-10489). Ice bullets: RESOLVED 2026-06-06. Iron-Knight ice breaks now call NativeRuntime::ice_block_bullets_loc_11052 before clearing the source cell, matching off_AFD8[2] -> IceBlock_SmashAndLoadBullets.
- **live fallback**: Metal push: berzerker_break_wall_block (crates/wildside-core/src/helmets.rs:6454-6506) only matches BlockType::Smash (line 6490) and clears Berzerker_charging; metal blocks are inert under a Berzerker charge, so chain-push is absent. Iron-Knight metal headbutt is a separate path that bounces the block in place (BlockBounceAnim, blocks.rs:3490-3507; lib.rs:3211+), not a push. Lift bob: live spawns LiftPlatform with y_velocity=-0x0001_0000 and steps it with step_lift_platform_sub_FCA6 (blocks.rs:1092, called from step_lift_platforms blocks.rs:3352-3365, spawn at blocks.rs:3606-3624). Functional rise is oracle-verified (backlog #067, #232) but the cosmetic block-bob animation is absent. Ice bullets: live in driller path apply_drilled_block_loc_3bede_3bef2 (blocks.rs:2233-2267) and Iron-Knight ice headbutt branch (lib.rs:3196-3228) after the 2026-06-06 wiring.
- **behaviour gap**: Three distinct sub-machines. (1) METAL-BLOCK PUSH = the Berzerker "moving block": ASM loc_111F4/sub_1129C (kid.asm:23130-23282) scans a horizontal run of metal blocks (collision $6000, type $500), then slides the chain 4px/frame for 4 substeps per block with sfx_Berzerker_moving_block, repeating into each adjacent solid metal cell until a non-solid neighbour or level edge, restoring tiles via sub_11530. The dark model implements this chain-slide; the live runtime never moves metal blocks. (2) LIFT-BLOCK BOB = ASM sub_FB3E/loc_FB94..FBDA (kid.asm:20905-20961): the visible block's GFX object bobs up/down (6/6, then 5/5, then 4/5 frames at 2px, hibernate-bracketed) before the platform rises. The dark model reproduces the bob delta tables; the live runtime spawns the functional rising LiftPlatform but plays no cosmetic bob. (3) ICE-BLOCK BULLETS = RESOLVED 2026-06-06 for Iron-Knight and Driller live paths.
- **symptom**: Berzerker charging into a row of metal blocks does not push the chain sideways (the "Berzerker moving block" mechanic is missing; blocks stay put). Lift blocks rise correctly but the block does not visibly bob up/down before lifting (cosmetic only). The former Iron-Knight ice-block ceiling-break symptom is resolved by wiring off_AFD8[2] to the existing `IceBlock_LoadBullets` model.
- **divergence evidence**: Read-only static trace; no emulator run launched (per instructions). (1) Metal push has no live caller (grep: only runtime_tests.rs); berzerker_break_wall_block handles only Smash, so a Berzerker charging a metal-block chain produces no horizontal slide. Strongly suspected to diverge, but no oracle artefact under .cache/native-oracle-runs or .cache/sweep-runs exercises a Berzerker-vs-metal-chain scenario, and the idle-scenario sweep would not trigger it. (2) Lift bob is cosmetic (GFX-object y only, no collision/platform-position effect): backlog #067/#232 closed the functional rise as oracle-matching, so the bob's absence is a visual/pixel gap, not a state divergence (fallback_clean at state level). (3) Ice-bullet headbutt gap is fixed in native and covered by `loc_af96_iron_knight_ice_block_loads_bullets_loc_11052`.
- **wiring sketch**: Remaining work: METAL PUSH: add a Berzerker-charge-into-metal trigger in berzerker_break_wall_block (helmets.rs:6488-6497) that, for BlockType::Metal, calls metal_block_push_entry_loc_111F4 -> metal_block_push_scan_right/left -> installs a worker driven each frame by metal_block_push_step_right/left_loc_112E2/112FE with the _delete_gate helpers and metal tile-restore; needs a new per-frame worker list (like lift_platforms/shooter_headbutt_workers). LIFT BOB: optional cosmetic; drive a block y_offset_px render field from lift_block_bob_deltas_sub_FB3E while the LiftPlatform is young; no state change.
- **refuter reasoning**: I independently re-derived all three sub-claims from the ASM (note: Bash `grep` was silently broken in this env; ripgrep was reliable and used for label verification).

(1) METAL PUSH: real state divergence. The Berzerker charge-into-wall dispatch is off_933E (kid.asm:10776), reached from loc_92EC (kid.asm:10735) under the `Berzerker_charging` gate (loc_92DE, 10729). Index 5 (Metal) = `j_loc_111F4` (kid.asm:10782) -> loc_111F4/sub_1129C (kid.asm:23130/23206): a real horizontal chain-slide of metal cells, 4px/frame x4 substeps per block, sfx_Berzerker_moving_block, repeating into adjacent $6000-collision metal cells, tiles restored via sub_11530. The live fallback `berzerker_break_wall_block` (helmets.rs:6454-6506) ONLY matches BlockType::Smash (line 6490) and clears charging; metal blocks are inert. dead-helper-census confirms `metal_block_push_entry_loc_111F4` has calls_nontest:0 (dark, test-only). This is a genuine engine-level state divergence: the block chain physically moves in ROM, stays put live. Not a redundant dark model.

(2) LIFT BOB: fallback_clean at state level. ASM sub_FB3E (kid.asm:20905) and the loc_FB94..FBDA bob passes operate on `$36(a5)` = a GFX object (a3), adjusting only y_pos(a3) by 2px in 6/6,5/5,4/5 hibernate-bracketed passes; no platform/collision-position effect. Functional rise is oracle-verified (backlog #067/#232) and lives via step_lift_platform_sub_FCA6. The bob's absence is a pixel/visual gap, not a state divergence. The investigator concedes this. Not worth wiring at state level.

(3) ICE BULLETS: real state divergence. off_AFD8 (kid.asm, Iron-Knight block dispatch) index 2 (Ice) = `j_IceBlock_SmashAndLoadBullets`. That routine calls `IceBlock_LoadBullets` and THEN spawns the cosmetic sub_10F9C. The live Iron-Knight Ice branch (lib.rs:3196-3210) spawns ONLY sub_10f9c and deletes the cell, emitting zero ShooterBlock projectiles. ripgrep confirms IceBlock_SmashAndLoadBullets's only explicit caller is Driller.asm:149 (the LIVE driller path), but the table-driven off_AFD8[2] also reaches it for Iron-Knight. Missing projectiles after an Iron-Knight ice-block break is a real spawned-object state divergence.

VERDICT: divergence_holds=true. Unlike the common "dark model whose fallback is already clean" error, here the live fallbacks are genuinely INCOMPLETE in state-affecting ways for two of three sub-machines (chain motion absent; bullets absent). I can independently stand behind those as engine-level divergences from the ASM ground truth.

CAVEATS lowering confidence to medium: (a) corrected divergence is suspected_diverges, NOT confirmed. The investigator launched no emulator run and NO artefact under .cache/native-oracle-runs/ (boot/title/walk/idle only) or the 105-level idle sweep exercises a Berzerker-vs-metal-chain or Iron-Knight-vs-ice-block scenario; the idle sweep never issues a charge/headbutt so it cannot trigger either path. (b) One of three sub-claims (lift-bob) is cosmetic-only / fallback_clean and should NOT be wired at state level. (c) A confirming oracle probe (Berzerker charging a metal chain; Iron-Knight headbutting ice) is required before promotion to confirmed_diverges.
- **leverage**: Two of three sub-machines (metal chain-push, Iron-Knight ice bullets) are genuine state-affecting fallback gaps, not redundant dark models, so worth wiring; lift-bob is cosmetic-only and not.

### 2. Boss state machines (boomerang/shishka/bagel multi-head + boss eye/death-burst/movement-script corpus)  `[SUSPECTED diverges]`

- **id**: `combat-bosses` · **status**: still_dark · **risk**: high · **effort**: large · **refuter verdict**: True (medium)
- **backlog**: #203, #205, #209, #217, #060, #055
- **ASM**: sub_39846, loc_37F30, loc_37F80, loc_37F94, loc_37FEA, sub_397E4, sub_3A292, loc_39478, sub_37332, loc_371B6, loc_32146
- **dead entrypoint**: boss_head_movement_step_sub_39846 at crates/wildside-core/src/combat.rs:6087 (base script stepper); boomerang_boss_head_1_init_loc_37F30 at combat.rs:2990; shishka_bagel_head_1_init_loc_39478 at combat.rs:3018; six head-movement wrappers calling the base stepper at combat.rs:6376/6402/6444/6487/6530/6572 (all dead-calling-dead)
- **live fallback**: crates/wildside-core/src/enemies.rs:9827 (EnemyArchetype::Tracker arm of step_active_enemies_with_rng) -> step_tracker at enemies.rs:26019 (flat chase: x_velocity +/-0x8000, y_velocity -0xB000 up / 0x4800 down, target 40px above player) + step_boss_fire at enemies.rs:26067 (hardcoded BOSS_FIRE_INTERVAL=180 frame timer, per-family projectile spawn with heuristic velocities). Boss families map to Tracker at enemies.rs:9071. The boss-head spawn/HP/offset bookkeeping (is_multi_head_boss enemies.rs:3496, boss_head_config:3504, boss_head_index field:6499) IS wired, but the per-head behavioural state machine is not.
- **behaviour gap**: The dark model is the ASM-faithful boss state machine: each boss head is a precise script. It sits in a hibernate/wait loop checking the Kid's Y is within a +/-$40px band (ASM loc_37F94 kid.asm:40353), faces the Kid, plays a wind-up animation (stru_39FC6), waits for an animation-frame gate ($18(a3), loc_37FEA), then fires a projectile via sub_397E4. Head movement advances from a fixed 16-entry (delay,x,y) script table (BOOMERANG_BOSS_HEAD_1_MOVEMENT_SUB_398F0) with FP16.16 conversion and a negative-delay rewind sentinel (sub_39846, kid.asm:42476). Fire cadence is animation/proximity-gated, not a clock. The live fallback instead chases at flat velocities and fires on a fixed frame timer.
- **symptom**: Bosses move and attack with the wrong cadence/trajectory: heads chase the player on a flat diagonal instead of following their fixed ROM movement scripts, and fire on a rigid 180-frame clock rather than the ROM's proximity-band + animation-gated attack, so projectile timing, aim, and head positioning diverge from the original boss fights. Gates any boss-fight TAS slice.
- **divergence evidence**: No boss oracle scenario exists. The idle sweep exercises no boss behaviour (backlog #205 explicitly: "the idle sweep exercises no boss / Diamond-Power-weapon / platform / weather behaviour"). The only boss artefact is scenarios.rs:2466 enemy_spawn_audit_heady_metal_targets_plethora_one, a pure-idle spawn-window audit (~120f, verifies the boss SPAWNS, not its movement/attack). No .cache/native-oracle-runs, .cache/sweep-runs, .cache/recordings or .cache/cases entry engages a boss head's movement/fire loop. Census (docs/source-port/dead-helper-census.md) verdict for combat.rs: 217/217 items unwired, "boss corpus has zero live refs". Confirmed via grep: boomerang_boss_head_1_init_loc_37F30 / boss_head_movement_step_sub_39846 / boss_eye_attack_step_sub_37332 / shishka_bagel_head_1_init have no callers outside combat.rs + sibling test files. Divergence is structurally near-certain (flat chase + 180f timer vs scripted-movement + proximity/animation-gated fire) but cannot be frame-confirmed cheaply without the #205 object-active harness, hence suspected, not confirmed.
- **wiring sketch**: Hook point: replace the EnemyArchetype::Tracker arm (enemies.rs:9827, currently step_tracker + step_boss_fire) with a per-boss-head state-machine driver keyed on a new boss_phase field in ActiveEnemy. Entrypoint: drive boss_head_movement_step_sub_39846(combat.rs:6087) each frame using the per-head movement table (BOOMERANG_BOSS_HEAD_1_MOVEMENT_SUB_398F0 combat.rs:6148) for movement, and the head wait/activation/attack-gate descriptors (boomerang_boss_head_1_wait_loop_loc_37F80, _activation_loc_37F94, _attack_animation_gate_loc_37FEA; shishka_bagel_head_* equivalents) to gate facing and projectile spawn via boss_head_projectile_spawn_sub_397E4 (combat.rs:2948). PREREQUISITE: build the #205 boss object-active DynamicScenario (warp to Boss1_LevelID=$10 / HeadyMetal level $33) with oracle state checkpoints first, or the wiring ships unverified against "oracle is truth".
- **refuter reasoning**: Independently verified all four legs of the claim. (1) ASM is genuinely scripted: kid.asm:40353 (loc_37F94) is a hibernate/Y-band machine: checks Kid Y within +/-$40 (addi.w #-$40/#+$40,d4; blt/bgt back to loc_37F80 wait), faces Kid via x_direction, plays wind-up anim stru_39FC6, gates fire on animation frame $18(a3) (loc_37FEA tst.b $18(a3); beq wait), then fires via sub_397E4; head movement runs from script table unk_398F0/sub_39846. (2) Live fallback is flat-chase: enemies.rs:9071 maps HeadyMetal/Shishkaboss/BoomerangBosses/BagelBrothers -> EnemyArchetype::Tracker; enemies.rs:9827 dispatches step_tracker (flat x_vel +/-$8000, y_vel -$B000/$4800, target 40px above player; enemies.rs:26019) + step_boss_fire (hardcoded BOSS_FIRE_INTERVAL=180 clock, heuristic per-family projectile velocities; enemies.rs:26067). Mechanism differs fundamentally: scripted movement-table + animation/proximity-gated fire vs flat velocity chase + fixed frame clock. (3) No boss oracle artefact: only boss scenario is scenarios.rs:2466 enemy_spawn_audit_heady_metal_targets_plethora_one, pure idle (all script bytes==0), checkpoints assert only spawn-window VISIBILITY (level_settle/enemy_spawn_window/visible_mid/visible_tail), never movement or fire. .cache/native-oracle-runs contains only boot/title/walk/level1_enemy_window, zero boss runs. backlog.md:1377 (#205) explicitly: idle sweep exercises no boss behaviour; the object-active harness needed to confirm does not yet exist. (4) Census (dead-helper-census.md:27) confirms combat.rs 217/217 unwired, boss corpus zero live refs. SKEPTICAL CHECK: this is NOT the redundant-dark-model trap. There is no oracle observation showing the fallback is adequate; the fallback is self-documented as heuristic (comment "heuristic velocities", hardcoded clock), not ASM-faithful. The investigator honestly labeled it suspected (not confirmed) precisely because it cannot be frame-confirmed without #205. The divergence is real in mechanism and structurally near-certain, so it survives the skeptical check and is worth wiring, but it is not yet frame-observable against any existing artefact, so confidence is medium and the corrected label stays suspected_diverges, not confirmed.
- **leverage**: High leverage: one sub_39846 stepper + per-head wrappers animates boomerang/shishka/bagel and gates the boss-fight TAS frontier; fallback is an admitted heuristic, not ASM-faithful.

### 3. Platform collision / carry / landing / overlap-resolution physics (Platforms_CheckCollision, kid.asm loc_257E..loc_2720)  `[SUSPECTED diverges]`

- **id**: `platforms-physics` · **status**: partially_wired · **risk**: high · **effort**: large · **refuter verdict**: True (medium)
- **backlog**: #208, #227, #203, #205, #231, #232
- **ASM**: Platforms_CheckCollision, loc_257E, loc_2590, loc_25A0, loc_2686, loc_26A2, loc_26B6, loc_26C0, loc_26D4, loc_26FE, loc_271A, loc_2720, sub_8ED0, loc_8DA0
- **dead entrypoint**: platform_landing_loc_26D4 + positive_platform_carry_loc_26A2 / negative_platform_carry_loc_26B6 / negative_platform_carry_commit_loc_26C0 / bottom_platform_carry_loc_26FE, crates/wildside-core/src/platforms.rs:330, 244, 297, 314, 356 (all still allow(dead_code), unreferenced by live code)
- **live fallback**: crates/wildside-core/src/platforms.rs:687 apply_platform_collision_with_ceiling_probe, called live from crates/wildside-core/src/lib.rs:3335 (step path). On-ground carry is additive velocity add (platforms.rs:778-781); airborne landing is a snap-tolerance top-landing approximation (platforms.rs:880-908). The high-level entry plus find_standing_platform_index_loc_8ED0 (lib.rs:3324/3355/3498) and the horizontal escape-magnitude helpers loc_25EE/2616/261E/2632/265A/266A/2686 (platforms.rs:835-877) ARE wired. The carry/landing state-machine helpers positive_platform_carry_loc_26A2 (platforms.rs:244), negative_platform_carry_loc_26B6 (297), negative_platform_carry_commit_loc_26C0 (314), platform_landing_loc_26D4 (330), bottom_platform_carry_loc_26FE (356) remain #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))] with zero non-test callers (only block_tests.rs:13601-13689).
- **behaviour gap**: The dark model is the ROM Platforms_CheckCollision carry/landing tail (kid.asm:4583-4637): after the smaller-axis escape wins, it (a) pushes Kid's hitbox by the signed escape and direction-clamps the carried platform velocity into $26(a0)/$2A(a0), keeping x-vel only when its sign matches the push side, else zeroing it (loc_26A2/26B6/26C0); (b) on a top landing clears y_vel, records the platform in Addr_PlatformStandingOn, sets FAA4 (loc_26D4); on a bottom hit copies the platform's $E(a2) y-vel plus a $4000 downward bias into $2A(a0) and sets FAA5 (loc_26FE); (c) sets FAA2-FAA5 directional contact flags and escalates to loc_271A (write #4 -> crush) when opposite-axis flags both fire. The live fallback instead carries velocity additively with no sign-clamp, snaps to plat_y-1 with floor-style sub-pixel logic, omits the $4000 bottom-face bias and bottom-face carry, never sets the FAA contact flags, and replaces the dual-axis FAA crush with a ceiling-probe heuristic gated on a block grid.
- **symptom**: On moving/falling/conveyor platforms Kid's horizontal carry is unclamped and only applies while grounded (never pushed out sideways when airborne against a platform side), top-landing sub-pixel and bottom-face behaviour differ (no $4000 downward bias, no bottom-face y-vel carry), and platform-squash/crush timing can differ at boundaries because the FAA dual-axis crush is replaced by a ceiling-probe heuristic. Net effect: platform-riding position/velocity can drift by a few px and crush deaths can misfire vs the ROM.
- **divergence evidence**: No moving-platform oracle scenario exists (only idle/walk runs in .cache/native-oracle-runs/: boot_title_idle_10s, boot_title_start_level1[_move_right_5s], level1_enemy_window, walk_right_3s; no platform/carry/conveyor run). The idle sweep exercises no moving-platform behaviour, so divergence is proven structurally (ASM-vs-native), not by an oracle frame diff. docs/source-port/platforms-fidelity-audit.md:53-66 documents the concrete divergences verified against kid.asm:4583-4637: (1) live horizontal carry adds platform x_velocity unconditionally/additively with no sign-clamp and only in the on-ground branch (platforms.rs:778-781), vs ROM loc_2686/26A2/26B6/26C0 push+direction-clamped carry into $26(a0); (2) live top landing snaps to plat_y-1 with floor sub-pixel logic and adds raw y_vel additively (platforms.rs:782, 893-906), vs ROM loc_26D4 clears y_vel + writes Addr_PlatformStandingOn + loc_26FE adds the $4000 bottom-face downward bias; (3) FAA2-FAA5 directional contact flags, FA96 jump-platform ref, and the loc_271A dual-axis crush escalation have no native state at all, so live crush is a ceiling-probe heuristic (platforms.rs:784-797). Backlog #208/#227 mark this P1 evidence-needed, blocked on the #205 object-active oracle harness. Could not cheaply settle with an oracle frame compare because building a moving-platform DynamicScenario that reaches live gameplay is exactly the #205 prerequisite that is still open.
- **wiring sketch**: Hook point: crates/wildside-core/src/platforms.rs:778-797 (on-ground additive-carry block) and the top-landing block at 893-906 inside apply_platform_collision_with_ceiling_probe (live from lib.rs:3335). Replace additive carry with: after the existing escape-magnitude selection (push_x/push_y already computed via the wired loc_25EE..2686 helpers), call platform_landing_loc_26D4 for a vertical-win top landing (apply push, zero y_vel, set standing platform), bottom_platform_carry_loc_26FE for a bottom hit ($4000 bias), and positive/negative_platform_carry_loc_26A2/26B6/26C0 for the horizontal-win carry. Requires adding FAA2-FAA5 contact-flag accumulator + Addr_PlatformStandingOn writeback to runtime state so loc_271A dual-axis crush can fire. PREREQUISITE: a #205-style moving-platform DynamicScenario with oracle checkpoints; do not wire blind (oracle is truth; idle sweep cannot verify this).
- **refuter reasoning**: I independently read the ground-truth ASM (kid.asm:4462-4642, Platforms_CheckCollision through loc_2720) and the live fallback (platforms.rs:687-911, wired from lib.rs:3335).

WHAT HOLDS (verified, not speculative):
1. The carry/landing tail helpers positive_platform_carry_loc_26A2 (platforms.rs:244), negative_platform_carry_loc_26B6 (297), negative_platform_carry_commit_loc_26C0 (314), platform_landing_loc_26D4 (330), bottom_platform_carry_loc_26FE (356) have ZERO live callers (grep confirms only block_tests.rs). The dark-model part is genuine.
2. On-ground carry (platforms.rs:778-781) does a plain additive x_pos += platform.x_velocity with no escape push and no direction-sign clamp, vs ASM loc_2686/26A2/26B6/26C0 which pushes the hitbox by signed escape d7 then carries $A(a2) into $26(a0) clamped to keep x-vel only when its sign matches the push side (else moveq #0,d7). Real algorithmic difference.
3. The loc_26FE +$4000 bottom-face downward bias and the bottom-face platform-y-vel carry are absent from the live path. Real.
4. FAA2-FAA5 directional contact flags and the loc_271A dual-axis crush escalation have no native state; live crush is a block-grid ceiling-probe heuristic (784-797). Real structural difference.

WHAT THE CLAIM OVERSTATES (so I lowered confidence and corrected to merely suspected):
- The airborne branch (platforms.rs:808-877) DOES implement the loc_25EE/2616/261E/2632/265A/266A escape computation, DOES compare horizontal vs vertical escape magnitudes (line 867), and DOES push Kid sideways via apply_horizontal_platform_push_loc_2686 (868). So "horizontal carry only in the on-ground branch / Kid never pushed sideways" is inaccurate for the airborne path; the magnitude/escape skeleton IS wired.
- The audit doc's hardcoded-half-width-5 gap (line 66) is stale: platforms.rs:715 passes current_form.half_width(), not 5.

DECISIVE SKEPTICAL CHECK (oracle-observability): I confirmed NO existing artefact exercises moving-platform carry. The only native-oracle-runs are title/idle/walk-right; the longest (move_right_5s) ends ~1019 frames into a rightward level-1 walk and the oracle state.json schema does not even record platform standing/velocity. So the divergence is genuinely NOT oracle-observable today, exactly as the investigator admits ("structural, not frame-diff"). I cannot independently produce an oracle frame diff; it is blocked on the #205 object-active harness.

VERDICT: This is NOT the common "dark model whose fallback is already oracle-clean" error to refute away. The fallback is demonstrably a different algorithm from the cited ASM (additive vs direction-clamped carry, missing $4000 bias, heuristic vs FAA-flag crush), so it would produce different physics the instant Kid rides a moving/trap platform. I set divergence_holds=true on those concrete code-level findings, but with medium confidence and corrected status "suspected_diverges" (not confirmed) because no oracle observation exists and parts of the claim (airborne escape, half-width) are overstated. Leverage is gated: not worth wiring until the #205 harness can demonstrate the frame diff.
- **leverage**: Real code-level divergences on the carry/landing tail, but gated behind a moving/trap-platform that no existing oracle run reaches; wiring needs the #205 object-active harness first, so worth it only once that harness lands.

It already replicates the dark manager's window gate (backlog #103 matched window bounds to loc_368A8; backlog #213 wired the loc_36900 inner-visible-window suppression via enemy_loading_initial_pass_complete and enemy_spawn_inside_visible_inner_window_loc_36900 at enemies.rs:8554) but uses killed_enemies permanence in place of the status-word countdown reload (combat.rs:8027). Evanescent-shooter spawn: step_shooter_blocks at crates/wildside-core/src/blocks.rs:3009 (wired at lib.rs:3429) runs its own inline shooter scan (cites loc_F09E/F0D0/F0D8/F106/F254) rather than calling the dark level.rs F1DE/F25C/F28C model.
- **behaviour gap**: The dark model implements a timed respawn/reload of killed enemies via the EnemyStatus_Table countdown ($2168 marker = bit-D countdown of ~360 frames, bit-E reload adding $400), plus a full ASM-faithful evanescent-shooter spawn/expire/visible-cell scan. The live fallback writes the respawn markers but never reads them, so killed enemies are suppressed permanently via a HashSet and shooters are spawned by a coarser inline scan.
- **symptom**: An enemy killed on Level 01 (or any level whose layout entry carries the respawn-marker status word) should reappear after roughly 360 frames once the camera re-enters its spawn window; live it stays dead for the remainder of the segment. Possible roster/number_objects drift and shooter-block timing/edge differences in dense shooter rooms.
- **divergence evidence**: Read of ASM Manage_EnemyLoading at .cache/upstream/kid-chameleon-disasm/kid.asm:37957-38099. The routine's heart is a per-entry EnemyStatus_Table status-word countdown: loc_36840 dispatches by word, loc_3685E counts down the $03FF low bits when bit-D ($2000) is set, loc_3686E does the bit-E reload incrementing by $400. The $2168 death marker (=0010000101101000b: bit-D set, low bits=$168=360) is therefore a ~360-frame respawn timer. LIVE: combat.rs writes that 0x2168 marker into self.enemy_status_words on every enemy death (apply_*_death_status_route_loc_3492C/3BC78 at combat.rs:8137-8174; respawn markers loc_3E97C/366A4/34188 in enemies.rs), but NOTHING in the live spawn path ever READS enemy_status_words back (grep: only fill()/get_mut() writes, never an indexed read in activate_enemies_*). Instead the live spawner gates respawns with a PERMANENT killed_enemies HashSet (combat.rs:8027 killed_enemies.insert; activate_enemies_with_rng_inner skips killed at enemies.rs:9353) that is cleared only on full level/segment reset (boot.rs:5684, level.rs:17897), never on a timed countdown. So a killed enemy never respawns live, whereas the ROM's status-word countdown can reload it after ~360 frames. I could NOT confirm a frame-exact oracle divergence from existing artefacts: no .cache/native-oracle-runs scenario (level1_enemy_window is an idle window with no kills) and no idle sweep scenario exercises kill-then-camera-re-enter-window, the only path that triggers the reload. Hence suspected, not confirmed.
- **wiring sketch**: Two independent, separable pieces. (1) Respawn-timer: in refresh_active_roster (enemies.rs:~40631, just before/inside the activate_enemies_with_rng_inner call) add a pre-pass over self.enemy_status_words that mirrors loc_36840: for each entry with bit-D set ($2000) decrement the low $03FF via manage_enemy_loading_count_down_active_loc_3685E, and when it reaches the spawn window clear the corresponding killed_enemies entry (or spawn directly through manage_enemy_loading_spawn_object_loc_3691E). This makes enemy_status_words an authoritative read, not a write-only field. (2) Shooter: have step_shooter_blocks (blocks.rs:3009) delegate its candidate scan to evanescent_shooter_scan_start_loc_F1C8 -> evanescent_shooter_cell_scan_loc_F1DE and active-slot stepping to shooter_active_slot_scan_step_loc_F28C, replacing the inline loc_F09E approximation. Prerequisite (per backlog #203): both need an enemy-active oracle scenario (kill + camera re-enter window for #1; a shooter-block level for #2) before wiring, or it ships unverified.
- **refuter reasoning**: Independent ASM check CONFIRMS the structural claim but the audit bar is "oracle-observable," which is NOT met.

What I verified independently:
1. enemy_status_words is write-only live. rg shows only fill()/get_mut() writes (boot.rs:5685, combat.rs:8144/8149/8163/8168, enemies.rs:40596) and never an indexed READ in any spawn path. The countdown logic at ASM loc_3685E/loc_3686E (kid.asm:37991-38017) that decrements (a2) and re-reads it is absent. Confirmed.
2. The live gate is the permanent killed_enemies HashSet (combat.rs:8027 insert; enemies.rs:9353 skip), cleared only on full level/segment reset (boot.rs:5684, level.rs:17897). Confirmed.
3. CRUCIAL ASM finding: $2168 is NOT a death-only marker. It is written by the SHARED enemy delete tail sub_3C3CE/loc_3C4C0 (kid.asm:43999-44017) and the generic Object_OutOfRange loc_320A6 (kid.asm:37487-37491) and per-family despawn checks (e.g. Lion sub_3E8BA/loc_3E97C, Lion.asm:855-932, which is a CAMERA-BOUNDS off-screen check, not a kill). Both kill and scroll-off-screen route through the same tail and write $2168 for positive $42 slots. The ROM has NO permanent "killed forever" flag in this loader: a killed enemy with positive $42 gets the ~360-frame countdown ($168=360, bit-D) and CAN reload (loc_3690A spawn). So the live permanent-suppression genuinely differs from the ROM's timed-reload model. The dark model is NOT redundant; the fallback is NOT already oracle-clean. The investigator's "combat.rs writes 0x2168 on death" framing is slightly imprecise (it is the shared kill/despawn tail), but the conclusion (live never reads it back, killed enemies never respawn live) is correct.
4. The lib.rs:96-97 field comment itself concedes this is an approximation: "Loader usage is still approximated by killed_enemies." Census confirms the per-family respawn-marker helpers are calls_nontest:0 (dead, test-only), e.g. lion_respawn_marker_loc_3e97c. Backlog #179/#182 explicitly list the $2168 respawn marker as "not wired."

Why divergence_holds=false despite a real mechanism gap: the audit standard is a real, ORACLE-OBSERVABLE divergence, and skepticism defaults to that higher bar. The investigator honestly rated this suspected_diverges and could NOT produce a frame-exact oracle artifact. I independently confirm none exists: level1_enemy_window is an idle/stomp window (PNGs at 0719-0820, no kill-then-rescroll), no sweep scenario exercises kill -> camera-leave->360+ frames->return, the only path that triggers reload. Triggering it requires a specific, possibly-rare in-normal-play sequence that is unproven against the oracle. The mechanism difference is real and ASM-faithful, but it remains speculative at the oracle level (suspected_diverges, not confirmed). Under the stated rule I cannot stand behind an oracle-observable divergence, so divergence_holds=false. This is a genuine architectural gap worth a probe BEFORE wiring, not a confirmed oracle bug that is currently worth wiring.
- **leverage**: Real ASM-grounded mechanism gap (timed respawn vs permanent HashSet), but unproven at the oracle; not worth wiring until a kill-then-rescroll scenario actually shows oracle divergence.

- **dead entrypoint**: sound_driver_begin_write_sub_E143A + the SoundDriver* family (sound_driver_write_sub_E1330, sound_driver_write_command_sub_E1482, sound_driver_write_byte_sub_E148E, sound_driver_write_pointer_sub_E14AC, sound_driver_upload_sub_E13DA, sound_driver_reset_sub_E1416, sound_driver_z80_handshake_loc_E136C, sound_driver_vdp_dma_wait_loc_E13B0, plus the E157E..E15E8 per-opcode emitters), crates/wildside-core/src/lib.rs:887 (and 572-705 for the structs)
- **live fallback**: crates/wildside-md/src/lib.rs:2884 GemsAudioEngine::play_sound (enqueue at wildside-md/src/lib.rs:2871 writing GEMS_QUEUE_ADDR=0x1A40 with head ptr at 0x0036). The live runtime runs a REAL Z80 emulator (use z80::{Z80,Z80_io}, wildside-md/src/lib.rs:11) that loads the actual GEMS_Sounddriver.bin into emulated Z80 RAM and drives a real YM2612+PSG synth (wildside-md/src/lib.rs:2652 "Standalone GEMS Audio Engine"). It implements the identical ring-buffer protocol end-to-end through hardware emulation at the same $A01A40/$A00036 offsets the dark model only describes. wildside-core's high-level sound state is tracked separately as QueuedSoundEffect/played_sound_effect_ids (combat.rs:39, trace.rs:5813) which carry the sound-id byte, not the bus protocol.
- **behaviour gap**: The dark model is a high-level structural transcription of the 68k-side GEMS ring-buffer writer routines: it would compute the byte sequences ([FF 05 id], [FF 0C], command+payload writes), the 6-bit ring index advance (wrapping_add & 0x3F), the Z80 bus request/grant handshake ($A11100 / $A01A20), the boot-time driver upload of GEMS_Sounddriver.bin into $A00000..$A02000, the reset delay loops, and the VDP DMA-busy wait during Z80 restart. It produces SoundDriver* result structs describing what bytes/indices the 68k would queue into the GEMS ring at $A01A40 (head byte $A00036). It does NOT synthesise audio; it is a pure descriptive model of the m68k-side queueing protocol.
- **symptom**: None attributable to this dark model. Live audio is produced by the wildside-md Z80/YM2612/PSG engine. Any residual audio gaps tracked under backlog #003 (intro/title/options BGM/SFX) are real-device/human-repro issues in the live synth path and would not be resolved by activating this descriptive 68k-queue model.
- **divergence evidence**: (1) rg confirms the entire SoundDriver* family is #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))] and referenced ONLY internally (model composing itself) plus from tests/boot_tests.rs and tests/combat_tests.rs, zero live callers. (2) Census docs/source-port/dead-helper-census.md:32,60-61,208,358 already flags this whole ~36-fn tree as "unwired, no live path emits a GEMS command" and explicitly raises the triage: redundant alt-impl (delete candidate) vs fidelity target. (3) The live path is the real hardware emulator in wildside-md (Z80 + YM2612 + PSG, GemsAudioEngine::play_sound at lib.rs:2884), which writes into the GEMS ring at the SAME 0x1A40/0x0036 offsets and runs the actual driver binary, and even carries its own ASM-cited tests (e.g. wildside-md/src/lib.rs:5454 "ASM sub_E14AC writes the low byte first..."). So the live audio path is itself the maintained, ASM-faithful implementation; the wildside-core model is a strictly-redundant second transcription of just the 68k queueing half. (4) Oracle DOES compare audio (verify_audio_output, wildside-cli/src/verify.rs:531; release_gate.rs:429; oracle helper writes audio.wav). Backlog #003 (docs/source-port/backlog.md:79) tracks audio under human/real-device repro, with the 2026-06-04 proactive sweep (846 diffs, all oracle_limitations, ZERO authoritative divergences) showing no actionable state bug. Audio divergence, where suspected, is a real-device-listening concern handled by the wildside-md engine, NOT something the wildside-core descriptive model could fix (it emits no samples).
- **wiring sketch**: No wiring recommended; this is a genuinely redundant alternative implementation, not a divergence-closer. The live wildside-md GemsAudioEngine already runs the real GEMS driver on an emulated Z80 and is the oracle-verified audio path; the wildside-core SoundDriver* model only describes the 68k-side byte-queueing and produces no audio. If one insisted on wiring, the hook point would be wherever wildside-core emits a sound (e.g. the QueuedSoundEffect -> sound_id() flow that feeds played_sound_effect_ids in trace.rs:5813) calling sound_driver_write_sub_E1330(sound_id) and routing the resulting queued_bytes, but that buys nothing the wildside-md engine does not already do correctly, and would duplicate state. Recommended disposition: treat as delete/keep-as-unit-tested-ASM-spec candidate, NOT wire. Cite census line 358 triage as resolved -> "redundant alternative impl".

(1) Subsystem misattribution. The claim says sub_F568 "feeds ROM block-collision tables that govern projectile spawn, barrier-ahead clearing, and player overlap/launch response." Reading the ASM contradicts this. sub_F568 (kid.asm:20196) has exactly one caller: `bsr.w sub_F568` at kid.asm:19865 (loc_F2B0), the tail of sub_F096 (kid.asm:19617). sub_F096 is the per-frame FOREGROUND-UPDATE / SPRITE-TABLE BUILD routine, gated by $FA64, reads Addr_GfxObject_Kid, computes a camera-relative block window, iterates the FG-update object list $F8C2, and writes Number_Sprites / Addr_NextSpriteSlot / FGUpdateQueueCell_NextSlot. It is called once per frame from the main loop (jsr (j_sub_F096).l, kid.asm:920). sub_F568 walks Kid's hitbox window and emits rectangles into the $F20A/$F2AA scratch buffers (kid.asm:20219-20220), which are sprite/FG occlusion rects for shooter-block sprites near Kid, a RENDERING concern. There is no ASM path from sub_F568 to projectile spawn, barrier clearing, or player launch. Those lifecycle behaviours run through the worker coroutines (loc_11430/sub_1149C/loc_11474) that the claim itself concedes are already wired live (lib.rs:3429/2724, blocks.rs:472/437). So even if sub_F568 were wired, it would not touch the symptoms #214 describes.

(2) No oracle-observable divergence. Backlog #214 (backlog.md:3746) is a human-playtest report with "Oracle repro: unknown" and "Native repro: not yet recorded." Every selector recording that could show a gap is stale with frame-1/3/4 source replay drift (backlog.md:3748-3804). The ONE current, green recording, issue-214-highwater-jump-overlap-current (421 frames), reports trace_match=true, oracle_state_match=true, oracle_frame_match=true, no frame diffs, and the backlog explicitly states "Do not patch #214 gameplay from this clean prefix" (backlog.md:3783-3784).

This is the classic dark-vs-wrong conflation: the model is genuinely dark, but it is a sprite-render helper, and the live fallback is oracle-clean on the only valid artefact. The claim's behaviour-gap narrative attributes collision/launch semantics to a routine the ROM uses for sprite occlusion. Suspected divergence does not survive a skeptical check; classification is fallback_clean. (Minor caveat: I did not trace the full downstream consumer of $F20A end-to-end, but its producer routine sub_F096 is unambiguously the sprite/FG-update builder, and the only valid oracle recording shows no divergence.)
- **leverage**: Not worth wiring: sub_F568 is a sprite-render helper, not a collision path, and the only valid oracle recording is clean.
